title: The Patient Herder
murle: Ngoki ci lo komo, ki cere anyo.
english: The one who waits quietly often finds the best pasture.
explanation: This proverb encourages patience and careful observation over rushed action, reflecting the herding lifestyle where waiting for the right moment brings greater reward.

title: One Stick Breaks
murle: Tit acen ki dirim, tit angun ki dirim ba.
english: A single stick breaks easily, but a bundle does not.
explanation: A reminder of the strength found in unity — individuals are vulnerable alone, but a community standing together is far more resilient.

title: The Elder's Shade
murle: Anyo lo mudho ki jalaba dirisi.
english: The shade of an elder shelters even those who did not plant the tree.
explanation: This speaks to the value of wisdom passed down through generations — the guidance of elders benefits the whole community, not only their immediate family.

title: Small Rain, Full River
murle: Ngoro cini ki bala, kori acen abu.
english: Even small rains, gathered together, can fill a great river.
explanation: Small, consistent efforts accumulate into significant results over time, encouraging patience and steady contribution rather than waiting for a single grand gesture.

title: The Quiet Path
murle: Woro ki lo bala, ki dhogo anyimo.
english: The quiet path often leads home safely.
explanation: This proverb favors humility and careful conduct over boastfulness, suggesting that a measured approach to life leads to lasting security.

title: Cattle and Kindness
murle: Loka ki bala, adhup ki komo ba.
english: Wealth in cattle fades, but kindness is never forgotten.
explanation: While cattle represent material wealth and status, this proverb reminds the community that acts of kindness leave a longer-lasting legacy than material possessions.
